A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiTMC study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original conformer-generation benchmarks, ensemble-property evaluations, generalization experiments and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds conditioning, model-scaling and accuracy-versus-runtime evaluations.

M1.justification: V2 removes the optional autoguided sampling extension in v1 Appendix J, which combines stronger and weaker models' velocity fields. The core DiTMC architecture, graph-conditioning mechanisms, positional embeddings, flow-matching objective and Euler sampler remain; bond-pair conditioning moves to Appendix I.2.

E1.justification: GEOM-QM9, GEOM-DRUGS, GEOM-XL and the SMILES classification tasks remain. However, v1 Appendix E.4/Table A12's evaluation of DRUGS-trained models on QM9 disappears, removing one cross-dataset generalization scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds MCF-S and MCF-B to the GEOM-DRUGS comparison in Table A10. It removes OMEGA from ensemble-property comparisons and GeoDiff and GeoMol from the GEOM-XL comparison. Most comparator families remain unchanged; ET-Flow's appearance in the main XL table promotes results already present in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a substantial accuracy-versus-runtime evaluation using 5, 10, 20 and 50 sampling steps on an A100 with batch size 128, including DDIM sampling for MCF (Appendix G.5). It also adds 1M-parameter aPE-S and large rPE configurations. Existing benchmark splits, thresholds, headline Euler sampling and training-budget rules remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds the DRUGS conditioning ablation and substantially expands scaling, coverage-threshold and accuracy-runtime analyses (Table 2; Figures 3-4 and A8-A13). It removes autoguidance sensitivity analysis, DRUGS-to-QM9 transfer analysis and PE(3) conditioning-ablation comparisons. Prior-choice, index-encoding, SMILES-classification and sampling-trajectory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averages and appendix standard deviations, including three sampled subsets for ensemble properties. V2 extends the same reporting practice to additional results without introducing a different run-count policy, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for rPE models, conditioning, small-model scaling and runtime budgets. For example, its new rPE-L DRUGS row reports mean COV-P of 78.1% and AMR-P of 0.466 Å (Table 3), while retained aPE-L scores remain unchanged. Transfer, autoguidance and several ablation/comparator results disappear. The main XL table also corrects aPE-B median AMR-P from 2.49 to 2.48 Å, matching v1's appendix.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the centering definition by adding the missing 1/N factor (v1 Eq. A22 to v2 Eq. A15) and adds 1/6 to the tetrahedron's oriented-volume formula. The equivariant positional-embedding and dot-product invariance proofs are relocated without substantive changes.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly adds the performance benefit of geodesic-distance attention conditioning to the introduction's contribution list and highlights GEOM-XL generalization in the conclusion. These refine the emphasis of existing findings; the abstract and overarching precision, physical-validity and symmetry-efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 proposes dataset/model co-scaling as an explanation for diminishing scaling returns and discusses physical validity without architectural equivariance. It adds substantive limitations concerning quadratic atom-count complexity and the conditioning redesign required for de-novo generation. The earlier interpretation of autoguidance's precision-diversity trade-off disappears.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-and-data archive link in Appendix N, specifications for additional model configurations and the A100 timing procedure. It corrects the swapped large-model parameter counts in v1 Table A10. The GitHub link and most training, preprocessing and sampling details already existed; these additions do not establish changes to retained implementations.

R1.justification: V2 adds de-novo generation and Uni-Mol positioning, including discussion of pair-representation costs, and references scaling laws, Euclidean fast attention, Kabsch alignment and RDKit. Autoguidance references and several positional-embedding/geometric-learning references are removed. The broader positioning as a modular molecular diffusion transformer remains.

P1.justification: Sections 4-5 are substantially reorganized and rewritten. Detailed attention equations move into Appendix D, bond-pair conditioning moves into the ablations, and the appendices regroup training, architecture, proofs and implementation material. V2 also adds a conference checklist and a dedicated availability section.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figure 3 and adds Figure 4, combining expanded comparisons with a reused molecular example. It adds extensive appendix threshold/runtime plots, removes the autoguidance plot, expands result tables and restructures XL results into parallel subset columns. The document adopts NeurIPS formatting; the architecture diagram and appendix molecular examples are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 supports its efficiency argument more directly through controlled accuracy-runtime comparisons (Figure 4; Appendix G.5), adds useful conditioning/scaling evidence, and corrects mathematical and reproducibility details. Removing the DRUGS-to-QM9, autoguidance and equivariant conditioning analyses reduces supporting breadth. The additions provide a limited net improvement to an already extensively evaluated paper.
